_comment: SWEG_MELEE_HOLD_OBJECTIVE — the melee 'score what you hold' late-game hold, the faithful fix for the Chaos Daemons objective-abandonment misplay found by reading the board (docs/PILOT_PROTOCOL.md). A Khorne melee force, tied on primary at the end of round 4 while CONTROLLING objectives, threw the decisive round 5 by walking its whole melee (Bloodcrushers / Flesh Hounds / Bloodmaster) OFF the markers it controlled to make a futile charge into a Toughness-12 Plagueburst Crawler for zero damage — surrendering the primary VP it was scoring for a brick it could not crack. This is an ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE PILOTING HEURISTIC composed with the already-cited core Objective Control rule (simulator.objective_control_strictly_greater), not a novel rules claim, registered here so the auditor tracks it (same class as simulator.staging_discipline / simulator.melee_caging). Lives entirely in code/strategy.py pick_move_intent, at the MELEE early-exit: in the scoring rounds (battle round 4 or 5), a MELEE-role unit that CURRENTLY CONTROLS the objective it is standing on (it carries Objective Control, own_oc > 0, and its army's summed OC on a marker within that marker's control radius strictly exceeds the enemy's — so leaving surrenders or reduces the control that is scoring primary) does NOT move off that marker toward the best melee target when that target is a durable brick it cannot crack (_is_caging_brick — Toughness 10 or higher, or 15 or more starting Wounds, the same brick definition simulator.antitank_advance_discipline and simulator.melee_caging use — AND one round of that unit's melee inflicts fewer than 1.0 wound on it via _kill_potential_wounds). Instead the unit returns a stationary HOLD (its own position, so control retention is guaranteed) and scores the primary. Four narrowings, each with a decisive rejection precedent: (1) it is a HOLD that keeps the unit SCORING on a marker it controls, NOT the charge-target redirect that screened SWEG_ELITE_ANTIBRICK at -7.63 and NOT the blanket charge-block that screened SWEG_AM_CHARGE_DISCIPLINE at -2.41 — the value is the retained primary VP, not a declined charge; (2) a unit controlling nothing charges/advances normally; (3) a crackable best target (not a brick, or one this unit can meaningfully hurt) falls through to the normal ENGAGE move — a winnable fight is never stopped; (4) it never triggers outside rounds 4-5, so early game the unit still commits forward. Faction-neutral. Default-off, byte-identical off: _melee_hold_objective_enabled() is the first short-circuit in the guard, so with the gate unset or '0' the MELEE early-exit returns its usual ENGAGE intent unchanged and no random numbers are drawn.

simulator.melee_hold_objective.rule_name: Objective Control (control an objective marker by having greater OC within range) — melee score-what-you-hold late-game hold
simulator.melee_hold_objective.quoted_text: Each model has an Objective Control characteristic ... While you control an objective marker, if a Primary Mission or Secondary Mission instructs you to score victory points for controlling objective markers, you can do so. ... An objective marker is controlled by the player that has the greater Objective Control characteristic total of models within range of that objective marker (i.e. within 3in horizontally and 5in vertically of it).
simulator.melee_hold_objective.trigger: SWEG_MELEE_HOLD_OBJECTIVE=1 (default-off; unset or '0' is the byte-identical kill-switch). In code/strategy.py pick_move_intent, at the MELEE early-exit, when ALL hold: the acting unit is MELEE-role; the live battle round (Battle._current_round) is 4 or 5; the unit carries Objective Control (own_oc > 0) and stands on an objective its army CONTROLS (its army's summed OC on a marker within that marker's control radius strictly exceeds the enemy's summed OC there); and the best melee target it would otherwise move onto is a durable brick (_is_caging_brick: Toughness 10 or higher, or 15 or more starting Wounds) that one round of this unit's melee cannot meaningfully damage (_kill_potential_wounds below 1.0 wound). If the best target is instead crackable, or the unit controls no marker, or the round is 1-3, the hold does not fire and the unit takes its normal ENGAGE move.
simulator.melee_hold_objective.effect: The unit returns a stationary HOLD (its own position) instead of the ENGAGE move onto the futile brick, so it keeps controlling the objective marker and scores the primary victory points it was already scoring, rather than surrendering that control to charge a target it cannot crack. Models the specific human decision the per-activation move planner omitted — 'I am winning the primary here, the only thing to charge is a brick I cannot hurt, so I stay and score' — the late-game score-what-you-hold trade real players make in the decisive rounds. It is scoped as a HOLD (retained primary VP), not a charge-target redirect (the rejected SWEG_ELITE_ANTIBRICK, -7.63) and not a blanket charge suppression (the rejected SWEG_AM_CHARGE_DISCIPLINE, -2.41): the unit is kept on the ground it is scoring, and a unit that controls nothing, faces a crackable target, or is in rounds 1-3 is untouched. Deterministic: the hold returns the unit's current position and draws no random numbers, so the gate-on arm consumes no extra RNG and the gate-off arm is byte-identical (the _melee_hold_objective_enabled() gate is the first short-circuit in the guard).
